related_questions.question: What is the best medication for type 2 diabetics?
related_questions.snippet: Metformin (Fortamet, Glumetza, others) is most often the first medicine prescribed for type 2 diabetes. It works mainly in two ways. It lowers the amount of glucose the liver makes. And it helps the body use insulin better.

related_questions.question: Which medication class is commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes?
related_questions.snippet: Biguanides. One commonly prescribed medication for type 2 diabetes is metformin, which belongs to a class of medications known as biguanides. This medication is taken daily by mouth. The medication makes your liver and muscles more sensitive to insulin and reduces glucose production in the liver.

text_blocks.snippet: Commonly used medications for type 2 diabetes include metformin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, and GLP-1 agonists, among others. Metformin is often the first-line treatment, while other medications like SGLT2 inhibitors may be considered based on individual needs and comorbidities.
snippet_highlighted_words: metformin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, and GLP-1 agonists

list.title: Metformin (Biguanides):
list.snippet: This is often the first medication prescribed and works by reducing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity.

list.title: Sulfonylureas:
list.snippet: These medications, such as glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide, stimulate the pancreas to release more insulin.

list.title: Thiazolidinediones (TZDs):
list.snippet: Pioglitazone is an example that enhances insulin's effectiveness in the body.

list.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists:
list.snippet: These injectable medications, like liraglutide and semaglutide, help lower blood sugar by increasing insulin release and reducing glucagon (a hormone that raises blood sugar).

list.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors:
list.snippet: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are examples of this class, which helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine.

list.title: DPP-4 Inhibitors:
list.snippet: Medications like sitagliptin and saxagliptin work by preventing the breakdown of a hormone that stimulates insulin release.

list.title: Insulin:
list.snippet: In some cases, especially when other medications are not enough, insulin injections or pumps may be necessary to manage blood sugar levels.

text_blocks.snippet: The best medication for a person with type 2 diabetes is determined by various factors, including their overall health, other medical conditions, and personal preferences. Healthcare providers consider factors like cardiovascular health, kidney function, and potential side effects when selecting the most appropriate medication.

list.title: Lifestyle Modifications:
list.snippet: Diet and exercise are crucial components of managing type 2 diabetes and may be used in conjunction with or as an alternative to medication.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: Regular monitoring of blood glucose levels is essential to assess the effectiveness of medication and make any necessary adjustments.

list.title: Side Effects:
list.snippet: All medications have potential side effects, and it's important to discuss any concerns with a healthcare professional.
